messages.subject: [amelia] Amelia: Problems with Step 3 - Output
messages.body_plain:
Hi Christina,

This is rather odd. It sounds like there might be a problem in your
installation of Amelia. You may want to try this first. Open R and run
the following two lines of code:

library(Amelia)
AmeliaView()

This should bring up the Amelia GUI. If this doesn't work, then
something is amiss and you should get back to us with a smidge more
detail--what operating system you are using, your version of R and
your version of Amelia You can find your version of Amelia by running
these two lines of code:

library(Amelia)
packageDescriptions("Amelia")

Also, are there text boxes next to the "Seed" text? Is there anything below it?

I'm sorry for all the bugs you're encountering, we'll try to get them fixed up.

cheers,
matt.

messages.subject: [amelia] R-sq and Amelia MI
messages.body_plain:
yes, you can do that if you think the R^2 is really a quantity of 
interest.  I'm skeptical that R^2 is something you should care about but 
any quantity you can calculate in one data set you can average in this way.
Gary

messages.subject: [amelia] Fixed Effects Regression
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I want to analyse the effect of several independent variables on the democratization process of almost every country in the world. At the same time I have 30 years for every country. 

1) Is there a possibility to do a fixed effects regression with my imputed datasets with Clarify (xtreg) or do I have to use Zelig?

2) If I have to use Zelig - what do I have to do or where can I find Information?

3) After this regression I want to use the synthetic control method. I don?t think that I can use the Imputed data sets for this. Is there a way to put the imputed datasets together in one dataset?

Can anyone help me figure out a way to get around this problems?

Thanks in advance for any help you can give.

Sincerely,

Laeticia Klein

messages.subject: [amelia] Fixed Effects Regression
messages.body_plain:
Laeticia,

	I did fixed/between/random effects regression for my own project, and  
I had to hand-write the code in R, as Stata's commands for MI data  
didn't do xtreg very well. As I wrote my quant chapter, nine months or  
so ago, Zelig only included GEE methods for panel data, which also  
didn't do what I wanted. So I had to write my own code in R.

	The code's not too hard (conceptually) to cook up, if you follow the  
algorithm in Gary's original article on MI. Also, I can dig out my  
code and share it if you decide you need it.

Best,
-Nathan

messages.subject: [amelia] Fixed Effects Regression
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I was working with imputed datasests once and I created dummies for
countries.  I supposed that was the easiest way to get FE estimation with
multiple imputed datasets.  Then I used "miest" and included the country
dummies in the regression...From reading your responses to Laeticia, I guess
what I did was wrong...is it?
Another thing that occurred to me, but it's incredibly time-consuming...And
I'm not sure it's right (please let me know if it's not): run the xtreg
regression on each of the imputed datasets.  Then averaged the coefficients
plus calculate the SE of each following the formula in Gary King et al.'s
paper...

If what I have done makes no sense at all....please let me know so that I
don't make the same mistakes again/.

thanks
Helen A Brown
